title: Year-end checklist: 5 numbers to pull before January

slides.headline: Before you plan 2027, pull these 5 numbers.
slides.body: One evening, a notepad, and your own systems. No consultant required. (Save this for the weekend.)

slides.headline: ① Calls: rings vs. answers
slides.body:
Pull your phone system's log for June–August. Total inbound vs. actually answered.
Healthy looks like: 90%+ answered. Industry average: ~27% missed. Every miss ≈ $500–$1,200.

slides.headline: ② Estimates: sent vs. closed
slides.body:
Last 90 days — quotes out the door vs. quotes that became jobs. Then count how many got a second touch.
Healthy looks like: 40%+ close rate. Typical: 25–30%, one follow-up or none.

slides.headline: ③ Reviews: you vs. your top 3
slides.body:
Google your main service + city. Write down the review counts of the top 3 shops, then yours.
Healthy looks like: you're within shouting distance. 91% of homeowners check reviews; half won't consider a shop under ~20.

slides.headline: ④ The list: customers you could text tomorrow
slides.body:
How many past customers with a working phone number/email live in your system? How many are on a maintenance agreement?
Healthy looks like: club members = 10%+ of the list and growing. Typical: big list, near-zero enrolled.

slides.headline: ⑤ Admin hours: the 9pm tax
slides.body:
Honest count — hours/week you (or your spouse) spend on invoicing, dispatch juggling, re-typing jobs between systems.
Healthy looks like: under 5. Typical: 10+.

slides.headline: These 5 numbers ARE the audit.
slides.body: Pull them yourself and you're 80% of the way there. Want the other 20% — the dollar figure per leak and the fix order? DM "AUDIT" in December. Enjoy the turkey first. 🦃
